newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait to launch second mobile phone company.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait to launch second mobile phone company.

text.p: Kuwait will launch in November a second mobile telephones firm, ending a monopoly by Mobile Telephone Company (MTC) to facilitate the privatisation of the sector, an official said on Tuesday.
"We cannot sell MTC now when it has a monopoly," the head of the state Kuwait Investment Authority (KIA) Ali al-Badr told Reuters in an interview.
"The new competitor company will be on the market in November. This will facilitate the shedding of government stakes in MTC and the new firm," he added.
He said the state, represented by its investment arm KIA, holds some 49 percent of MTC's shares and will have a stake of between 25 percent and 40 percent in the new firm.
MTC shares were trading around 990 fils ($3.25) on Tuesday on the Kuwait stock exchange compared with a high earlier this year of 1.180 dinars. There are 1,000 fils in a dinar.
Badr said KIA had sold stakes in 22 listed and unlisted firms since the launch of the first phase of the privatisation programme in September 1994 for 740 million dinars.

The government's shedding of shares has more than tripled trading volume and value over the past year on the Kuwait Stock Exchange to weekly averages of some 900 million shares worth 190 million respectively.
